==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|desir}}, {{m|enm|desire|pos=noun}} and {{m|enm|desiren|pos=verb}}, from {{der|en|fro|desirer}}, {{m|fro|desirrer}}, from {{der|en|la|dēsīderō|t=to long for, desire, feel the want of, miss, regret}}, apparently from {{m|la|de-}} + {{m|la|sidus}} (in the phrase ''de sidere'', "from the stars") in connection with astrological hopes. Compare {{m|en|consider}} and {{m|en|desiderate}}. The verb, along with Old Norse derived {{m|en|want|pos=verb}}, has mostly replaced native {{m|en|will|}} in modern English.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|dĭ-zīrʹ|dĭ-zīʹər|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/dɪˈzaɪə/}}
* {{enPR|dĭ-zīrʹ|dĭ-zīʹər|dē-zīrʹ|dē-zīʹər|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/dɪˈzaɪɹ/|/dɪˈzaɪɚ/|/diˈzaɪɹ/|/diˈzaɪɚ/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-desire.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-desire.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{hyphenation|en|de|sire}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪə(ɹ)|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To [[want]]; to wish for earnestly.
#: {{ux|en|I '''desire''' to speak with you.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Exodus|34|24|passage=Neither shall any man '''desire''' thy land.}}
#* {{RQ:Tennyson Idylls|edition=cabinet|volume=VI|poem=Lancelot and Elaine|page=88|passage=[S]eeing you '''desire''' your child to live, / Thanks, but you work against your own desire; {{...}}}}
# To put a [[request]] to (someone); to [[entreat]].
#* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|Acts|XIII|text=And when they founde no cause of deeth in hym, yet '''desired''' they Pilate to kyll him.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=III|page=15|passage=Mr. Barrett, however, by fawning and flattery, seemed to be able to make not only Mrs. Churchill but everyone else do what he '''desired'''.}}
# To want [[emotionally]] or [[sexually]].
#: {{ux|en|She has '''desired''' him since they first met.}}
# To express a wish for; to entreat; to request.
#* {{RQ:King James Version|2 Kings|4|28|passage=Then shee said, Did I '''desire''' a sonne of my Lord ? did I not say, Doe not deceiue me?}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|act=IV|scene=vii|passage='''Desire''' him to go in; trouble him no more.}}
# To require; to demand; to claim.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1580|author=w:Edmund Spenser|title=The Teares of the Muses
|passage=A doleful case '''desires''' a doleful song.}}
# To [[miss]]; to [[regret]].
#* {{RQ:Taylor Eniautos|passage=She shall be pleasant while she lives, and '''desired''' when she dies.}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The feeling of desiring; an eager longing for something.
#: {{ux|en|Too much '''desire''' can seriously affect one’s judgement.}}
#* {{RQ:Forster Angels|chapter=7|passage=He stood...filled with the '''desire''' that his son should be like him, and should have sons like him, to people the earth. It is the strongest '''desire''' that can come to a man - if it comes to him at all - stronger even than love or the desire for personal immortality.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} Someone or something wished for.
#: {{syn|en|pleasure|mind}}
#: {{ux|en|It is my '''desire''' to speak with you.}}
#: {{ux|en|You’re my heart’s '''desire'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-07|author=David Simpson
|volume=188|issue=26|page=36|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/books/2013/may/18/falling-upwards-richard-holmes-review Fantasy of navigation]
|passage=It is tempting to speculate about the incentives or compulsions that might explain why anyone would take to the skies in [the] basket [of a balloon]: perhaps out of a '''desire''' to escape the gravity of this world or to get a preview of the next; […].}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Strong attraction, particularly romantic or sexual.
#: {{ux|en|His '''desire''' for her kept him awake at night.}}
#* {{quote-av|en|year=1972|writer=w:Jay Presson Allen|title={{w|Cabaret (1972 film)|Cabaret}}|role=w:Sally Bowles|actor=w:Liza Minnelli|passage=Doesn't my body drive you wild with '''desire'''?}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[motivation|Motivation]]. {{rfex|en}}
